note: Rows for the twenty-two shell findings that had no queue row. Renames append the claim to the board that answers the finding — the apply-truth-marks idiom this arc already uses — because an add-board row never reaches queue-state and therefore never credits the register: eleven boards were built on 2026-09-07 and every finding they answer still read PENDING. Every expect string is the board's exact current name, read back from page 1:3 on 2026-09-07.

rows.reason: UX-F-17 — page management exists twice (PageTabBar.tsx:212-410 vs PagesTab, plus a third picker at PageCommandPalette.tsx:140). SPEC-NAVIGATION §7 settles ownership in as many words: “the duplicate is real (UX-F-17, UX-B-15) and it is the Pages spec’s decision, not this one. This spec only asks that the two strips stop reading as one list.” Re-read at HEAD 2026-09-07. The half that IS navigation’s — the two tablists reading as one — is drawn on 2844:12121 and credited under UX-F-16. Drawing a shell answer to who owns page management would pre-empt section 04 · Pages (1776:8377).

The six Notifications boards in section 1779:2 are all drawn 280 wide (165:2, 165:24, 165:44, 165:51, 165:71, 453:4051 — read back 2026-09-07 at 280x812 on a 400 pitch). The shipped dropdown is 360. A frame resize alone would leave a 280 interior inside a 360 box, which is a worse drawing than the one that ships, so this is a re-layout for someone with a cursor and not a resize row. The class statement is on 165:2’s name and on 963:4474. (UX-F-26, UX-F-25)
